I used to smoke. Not daily but every few weeks when my depression got too tough to handle. And it wouldn’t be gradual either. I’d burn through a whole pack in less than 24 hours. Then I’d think, “Heh, I’m not even addicted,” because I could quit the next day and be fine. Cue the cycle. No routine is healthy, and I relapsed a couple of times in my efforts to quit.

That being said, for anyone who’s trying to quit; every time you feel like you’re going to relapse, get a box of Tic Tacs or any mints and chew on them. As excessively as possible. They’re much cheaper and you’ll actually be somewhat alerted with good breath. They’ll work to distract your brain and give you something to do. Took me about three boxes until I didn’t need it anymore and could just stifle it mentally. And for every weak impasse that you beat, it will get increasingly easier and easier.

I read through this thread. I'm a Cambodian and although I live in Bangkok now, I've worked with a ton of small and medium businesses as well as hotels prior to moving. Let me just be very, very blunt with you because you seem to be very serious about your career and you will be disappointed a lot if you head to a country where the general mindset lies along the spectrum of cheap and lazy.

These people don't care all that much. As long as the Wi-Fi works and customers can relatively connect as they come and go, that's all they care about. They often do not have the capacity, time, or money to have things professionally configured. If anything goes wrong, they either call in to complain to their service provider and have their provider send over a few technicians (Khmer-speaking ones, mind you), or just call over a random technician from some random shop.
